title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the instruction-sheet direction. Keep it, take a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Instruction Sheet
options.thesis: ModelView reads like the folded sheet in a kit box: numbered callouts, ruled panels, one stamped verdict.
options.viewport: Paper chrome around a dark inspection stage; numbered roundels key every defect to a ruled checklist.
options.risk: Reads document-like if the viewport is not allowed to dominate.

raised.raise: Selection is unmistakable: the focused object lifts while the rest of the scene and list dim a step.
Defect callouts register to the viewport frame with crosshair ticks, so no mark floats free of the model.
The verdict stamps onto the report and persists; closing a panel never erases a state.
The inspection layer never edits the terrain: defect marks sit on a togglable layer above the mesh.

options.label: Constructed Grid
options.thesis: A visible construction grid under every screen; measurements are the interface.
options.viewport: Light stage on a blue 10 mm grid; bbox corners carry crosshair registration and dimension lines.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: a print inspector is a measurement surface, and the visible grid earns its place. Loses on maker-world warmth.
options.risk: White-and-blue precision can drift into generic technical software.

options.label: Emission Rail
options.thesis: One calibrated rail holds every check; state is carried by line height, dash and doubling, not hue.
options.viewport: Near-black stage with a hairline plate; defect types appear as thin spectral lines and a legend strip.
options.case: Fuses well for defect states and night-desk use; the spectroscope itself is not maker culture.
options.risk: Reads as an instrument costume if the rail stops doing real work.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain as a fixed colour language, the active route as a purple overlay.
options.viewport: A layered map where each inspection pass is a course leg over the model.
options.case: Loses both: makers do not identify with orienteering, and a 3D mesh is not terrain.
options.kept: A separate overlay layer that never edits the terrain.

options.label: Plate Section
options.thesis: Near-white stock, registration crosshairs, letterpressed attribution.
options.viewport: A continuous printed sheet with plate-corner crosshairs and hairline credit rows.
options.case: Loses on product clarity: the page furniture outranks the model.
options.kept: Registration crosshairs that tie a mark to the frame.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles; the focused tile grows and everything else dims.
options.viewport: Objects as a wall of poster tiles, one expanded on focus.
options.case: Loses both: the metaphor is browsing titles, not inspecting a mesh.
options.kept: Focus that lifts one object and dims the rest.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Carbon-copy coupons; every state stamps itself and nothing disappears.
options.viewport: The file as a coupon book, one inspection leg per sheet.
options.case: Loses on identification: a hobbyist inspects a model, not a journey.
options.kept: States persist as stamps rather than vanishing.
